subject: Mid-quarter: product & infra OKR alignment and dependency commitments
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-quarter check-in: product & infra OKRs (action items)

Hi all,

Quick mid-quarter pulse on the product + infra OKRs (attached: midq_snapshot_v2.pdf, okr_tracker_q3.xlsx). I kept this intentionally short — goal is to land decisions and owners by next week so QBR prep isn't scrambled. Highlights: 

- Product roadmap OKR (Improve inference throughput): yellow. Compression prototype is working but end-to-end latency regressed on longer contexts.
- Infra OKR (Sustained 95th pctl SLAs on p3/rt): amber. We have a kernel optimization backlog and limited GPU spin-up slots.
- Sales & Field ask (AtlasHealth): they need a predictable SLA timeline for pilot next month.

Two concrete asks: 
1) Re-scope option & decision: I drafted two re-scope options in the linked doc (summary below). Need a decision so we can lock engineering headcount for 2-week focused sprint.
2) Dependency commitments: infra to confirm whether two engineers can be shifted for a focused unblock window; product to confirm whether we can postpone the new defaults UI push by 3 weeks.

Rescope options (summary):
- Option A (ambitious): Finish compression + kernel work now, preserves full feature set, needs 2 infra engineers for 3 weeks and extra procurement (GPU capacity).
- Option B (pragmatic): Ship partial compression + caching improvements, delay defaults UI, preserves latency SLOs for most customers, needs 2 infra engineers for 2 weeks and minimal procurement.

Please reply with: 
- Which option you prefer (A/B)
- Whether infra can commit engineers and tentative dates
- Any blockers I should escalate to leadership this week

Target: owners commit by EOD Friday 2026-09-03. If we can't get alignment, we'll default to Option B and prioritize AtlasHealth gating criteria.

Thanks — short meeting if helpful, but prefer async unless major objections.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — good concise summary.

Quick thoughts: lean toward Option B given capacity constraints on procurement and the front-loaded risk of full compression in Option A. We can hit AtlasHealth pilot if we preserve their gating criteria and accept a slightly reduced default experience during the pilot.

On infra commits: I can push to free up one backend engineer immediately and coordinate procurement conversations, but I need rohan to confirm whether we can reassign the additional headcount without impacting Q3 commitments for the feature roadmap.

@Rohan — can you weigh in on shifting a second engineer and any timeline constraints?

-V

Appreciate the summary and the clear asks. My read: Option B is the lower-risk path and aligns with AtlasHealth's immediate needs, but we should formalize canary gating for latency/quality so the pilot doesn't create churn. I reviewed the doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1y2MidQ-RescopeOptions) and suggest the following additions before we lock Option B: 

- Canary criteria (pre-launch): 95th pctl latency within 1.2x baseline on the 50–75 token distribution; pass three regression prompts (shared in the doc).
- Rollout plan: 50% traffic limit for pilot, automated rollback if error rate >1.5% or latency > target for more than 10 minutes.

Notes on timeline: if infra can confirm the 2-week focused window starting 2026-09-13 for kernel + KV cache work, we can hit the pilot start target. If we can't get that window, we need to set expectations with AtlasHealth for a late-October pilot.

@Karthik — need your confirmation that the canary checks are implementable on the current tracing hooks.

-Naomi

- Commitment: 2 infra engineers for a 10 business day focused sprint starting 2026-09-13. Priority will be kernel optimization and KV cache stabilization.
- Procurement: we'll expedite an add-on GPU pool with CloudFabric; procurement expects a signed SOW and PO by 2026-09-10 to guarantee capacity. I've looped in Procurement contact (procurement@cloudfabric.com) offline.

Thanks everyone — quick consolidation and next steps: 

Decision: we will proceed with Option B (pragmatic re-scope). Rationale: minimizes customer risk for AtlasHealth pilot while keeping delivery tractable for Q3.

Owners & commitments: 
- Infra (Karthik): 2 engineers, focused sprint 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-24. Track in SUP-1982. Please confirm names by EOD 2026-09-10.
- Product (Vanessa): delay defaults UI rollout by 3 weeks; finalize canary prompts with Naomi by 9/09.
- Program (Rohan): draft comms to AtlasHealth + internal QBR blurb and confirm that delaying defaults doesn't impact other pilots.
- Procurement: CloudFabric to provide SOW/PO template; procurement@cloudfabric.com please send next steps (I've added you to the thread).

Follow-up: schedule 30m async readout/call 2026-09-14 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=redwood-midq-followup-20260914.

If any of the commitments above can't be met, flag it in this thread immediately so I can escalate to leadership. Otherwise I'll update the OKR tracker and QBR deck with the decision and owners.

Thanks — will share the updated one-pager after I fold in Karthik's dates.

Best,
